rejected.title: Building an interpretation
card: An interpretation is a reasoned view of what a text means. It goes beyond what happens and says what the text suggests about people, ideas or the world.
It is built from a pattern of evidence. A pattern is something that repeats or links across the whole text, such as a recurring image, a character's repeated choices or a shift in tone.
One quote or one scene is not enough, because it may be an exception. Evidence from the beginning, middle and end shows the view holds across the text.
A strong interpretation is a claim that can be argued, and it explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rejected.remember: An interpretation is a reasoned claim about meaning, backed by patterns of evidence from the whole text.

a.q: Which of these is an interpretation of an invented novel about a lighthouse keeper?
opts: The novel shows that isolation helps people face themselves
The novel shows the keeper living alone on a rocky island
The novel shows a storm waking the keeper in chapter one
The novel is told in twelve chapters across one winter
a.why: The option about isolation helping people face themselves is a claim about what the novel means, and a reader could argue for or against it using evidence. The storm option is tempting because it uses the same words, but it only reports an event that anyone can check in the book.
a.clue: Which option could two readers disagree about?

b.q: Priya says an invented novel shows that loyalty can be a trap. Which evidence would best support her view?
opts: Early, middle and late characters are each harmed by loyalty
One character is loyal to a friend in chapter two
The author uses short sentences in the opening chapter
The title names a faithful dog that appears once
b.why: Her claim is about the whole book, so it needs a pattern across several points in the text. A single loyal act in chapter two is tempting, but one instance may be an exception and does not show a pattern.
b.clue: Look for evidence that repeats across the text.
